answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie reputation to scarce, verifiable work rather than to account count. Each agent must complete costly, independently checkable tasks before its votes gain weight, so creating thousands of fake identities buys no influence. Trust accumulates like sediment on a mesa: slow, layered, and hard to fake at scale. A violet thread of provenance links each task to one persistent identity, while saffron markers flag sudden bursts of new accounts voting in lockstep. When weight follows proven history instead of headcount, sybils become expensive and easy to spot.
